correctness.rationale: Re-audited the nonbinary theorem in /workspace/repairs/2/RESULT.md. The spectral bright space is the orthogonal sum of the spans of the two projected absorbers at each eigenvalue. Its complement is a direct sum of annihilated eigenspace components, not necessarily composed of individual adjacency eigenvectors as the frozen proof wording could suggest. The two spaces reduce adjacency and loss. On the bright space, taking the inner product of an effective eigenvector with its eigenvalue equation rules out zero imaginary part by positivity and the definition of the complement; all its Jordan components decay. This proves U†U tends to the dark projector and gives the exact trace identity even for coherent density matrices. The tensor projectors C=J/q and D=I−J/q furnish the q-ary Krawtchouk kernel with normalization q⁻ᵈ. At every nonconstant level k, K_k(h)/B_k is the mean of (−1/(q−1))^J for the number J of differing positions in a uniform k-subset. Because h≥1 and q≥3, J>0 has positive probability and those summands have modulus below one, proving strict rank two even at k=d and for composite q. The constant level contributes one dimension and q⁻ᵈ to the site law. Gram inversion gives the sitewise formula; tracing recovers the uniform mean, and removing the two certain-absorption vertices gives the conditional mean. For d=1 the nonsink probability is 1/(q−2); q=3,d=1 is full absorption. Independently evaluated the H(2,3) example with exact fractions, giving 3/5 and 2/5 with unchanged average 5/9. The frozen binary formula is also mathematically sound: for h=d all k-subsets give the same sign, while for 1≤h<d interior k allow both signs; its adjacent case splits off the first coordinate, and d=1 is two fully absorbing vertices. The submitted numerical checker was inspected, not executed; its finite scope is reported in the repair.

evidence: 1660beea2236 gives the exact 2d+1 rank and three-distance cosine law for primitive distance-regular graphs; 9174c1f874d0 gives rank five and the analogous site law for primitive strongly regular graphs. Both are November 2 records. Novo et al. give the single-absorber hypercube Krylov computation; Razzoli et al. treat single traps and identify multiple-trap placement as a direction for further work. Coutinho–Godsil–Guo–Vanhove Theorem 4.1 treats a necessary condition for unitary perfect transfer, not the two-loss projection ranks.
broader_coverage.reasoning: For q≥3, every distance-h graph of H(d,q) is connected: in the additive word model, differences of two length-h steps that use the same support and values except for 1 versus 2 in one coordinate generate the unit changes. Thus the November 2 primitive distance-regular result genuinely implies the nonbinary rank and, on inserting the Hamming kernel, the site formula. The diameter-two case is also covered by the later primitive strongly regular theorem. These later results do not supply earlier priority, and unitary transfer alone does not imply noncollinearity at every nonconstant level.

evidence: e6d55236b096 states survival s(x), exactly 1−η(x), with the same binary Krawtchouk Gram expression and rank split. Strong cospectrality means P_k e_u=±P_k e_v for every level, equivalent here to rank one in every block; failure at some level alone does not determine the total rank. The usual walk matrix from the single sum e_u+e_v is not the two-input block Krylov matrix.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The two-input rank is equivalent to the rank of the combined separate Krylov spans, not to a single-vector sum or a perfect state transfer probability. The October 12 binary result is equivalent coverage despite the complementary survival convention and rate normalization.

originality.rationale: The frozen originality claim FAILS as written: its two-absorber binary ranks, antipodal redundancy and binary sitewise law were already explicitly published in Resultary e6d55236b096, dated October 12. The d=1 endpoint and adjacent-binomial simplification do not rescue novelty for that branch. The revised result removes the binary branch from the Finding, explicitly credits it, and re-audits the nonbinary rank and sitewise law already contained in the October 27 evidence. The closest same-family and stronger distance-regular absorption records located for that retained claim are dated November 2, and are acknowledged as mathematical coverage, not preemption of the October 27 nonbinary finding. No novelty is claimed for the abstract spectral-projection method or for the boundary check d=1 in isolation.
residual_risks: An older two-input controllability or association-scheme specialization could supply the nonbinary ranks and explicit probabilities. The inspected general papers do not settle that possibility.
The novelty determination concerns retained content of the October 27 finding, not a claim of first discovery at the date of this repair. The later primitive and Hamming overlaps are explicit.

value.rationale: The nonbinary theorem independently solves the two-site placement question on a natural infinite family, including composite alphabets. Every nonconstant spectral block has two independent capture directions, explaining why placement cannot change the overall average, unlike the prior binary obstruction. The explicit site law also separates placement invariance of the mean from placement sensitivity of local capture, as the exact H(2,3) example shows. This is not novelty assigned to the old binary ranks, their small edge cases or a generic rewriting of Gram inversion.
